qa_pairs.instruction: Why can't multiple JDBC driver instances that require different versions of the same third‑party driver run in the same Java Virtual Machine?
qa_pairs.output: In the JDBC driver, different versions of the same third‑party classes (such as the Oracle JDBC driver or IBM DB2 Type 3 JDBC driver) collide when loaded in the same JVM, causing class conflicts that prevent both instances from operating correctly.

qa_pairs.instruction: How do you run multiple JDBC driver instances in the same driver set when each instance needs a different version of a third‑party JDBC driver?
qa_pairs.output: In the JDBC driver, use the Remote Loader to load each JDBC driver instance in a separate Java Virtual Machine (JVM). Loading each instance in its own JVM isolates the different third‑party driver versions and avoids class collisions.

qa_pairs.instruction: What problem occurs if you try to run multiple JDBC driver instances with different versions of the same third‑party driver in a single JVM, and how can you fix it?
qa_pairs.output: In the JDBC driver, attempting to run multiple instances that require different versions of the same third‑party JDBC driver in a single JVM results in class version collisions. The fix is to employ the Remote Loader so that each JDBC driver instance runs in its own JVM, thereby separating the conflicting classes.
